bug_semantics: On a WolfStack node still using the published built-in cluster secret, an unauthenticated remote client could send that constant in X-WolfStack-Secret. The pre-25.9.2 validate_inter_node_secret() accepted it without constraining the transport peer, and require_auth() returned the privileged synthetic identity cluster-node without a session, API key, or account. A caller reaching the management port could therefore enumerate Docker/LXC containers and invoke POST /api/containers/{runtime}/{id}/exec, whose handler passed attacker-controlled command text to sh -c inside the selected container. The 25.9.2 fix routes every presentation of the built-in default through a transport-peer gate and accepts it only from an address already recorded in nodes.json; custom per-installation secrets remain valid normally.
flaw_origin: Commit 2d2d371527bde1e9d72eadcd2ee3e7c0ee3adfbc (v5.9.4) is the smallest true first-writer of the hard-coded credential. It deliberately replaced the parent revision's per-node /etc/wolfstack/cluster.key loading and two-UUID random generation with the source-visible CLUSTER_SECRET constant and made load_cluster_secret() return that same value on every installation. The header gate itself came from the immediately preceding v5.9.3 commit and was not vulnerable there because its expected secret was independently generated per node. The constant was temporarily removed by the 11.26.3 hardening and restored by the 11.26.4 revert, but the revert is a later carrier/reintroduction, not the first BIC; subsequent rotation/migration work retained the built-in value as an accepted fallback on unmigrated nodes until 25.9.2.
ai_marker: Absent on BIC 2d2d371527bde1e9d72eadcd2ee3e7c0ee3adfbc. `git cat-file commit` shows human author and committer Paul C <paulc@wolf.uk.com>, the v5.9.4 subject/body, and no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, AI, bot, or agent trailer/identity.
evidence: First-party advisory https://github.com/wolfsoftwaresystemsltd/WolfStack/security/advisories/GHSA-r3mw-2wmq-j6jg states affected <=25.9.1, patched 25.9.2, identifies affected built-in-default configurations, the X-WolfStack-Secret -> require_auth() -> cluster-node path, the container exec impact, and the recorded-transport-peer fix. In the assigned clone: `git log --all --reverse -S'<full wsk_a7...f1a3 constant>' -- src/auth/mod.rs` first returns 2d2d371527bde1e9d72eadcd2ee3e7c0ee3adfbc; later hits are the temporary 11.26.3 removal and 11.26.4 revert. `git log -L '/^const CLUSTER_SECRET/,+1':src/auth/mod.rs` traces the same lineage back to 2d2d371. `git show 2d2d371^..2d2d371 -- src/auth/mod.rs src/main.rs` shows the random per-node key implementation deleted and the universal literal/return inserted. `git show a05c0870a84981d639067719de6be2395c958852:src/auth/mod.rs` directly verifies the parent instead reads /etc/wolfstack/cluster.key or generates two UUIDv4 values and contains no hard-coded default. `git grep -n -A45 'pub fn require_auth' v25.9.1 -- src/api/mod.rs` shows X-WolfStack-Secret passed to validate_inter_node_secret and success returning cluster-node; `git grep -n -A55 'pub async fn container_exec' v25.9.1 -- src/api/mod.rs` shows require_auth followed by container_exec_cmd(..., ['sh','-c',cmd]). `git grep -n -A75 'pub fn validate_inter_node_secret' v25.9.1 -- src/auth/mod.rs` shows acceptance through the in-memory, on-disk, or built-in-default branches, while default_secret_accepted() returns true on an unmigrated node unless explicit rejection is configured. `git show 3767540356e16130717abe4d7846bd5a20eae71b` changes Cargo.toml 25.9.1 -> 25.9.2, adds peer_ip() based on HttpRequest::peer_addr(), replaces all 14 validation call sites with validate_inter_node_secret_from(..., peer), and forces the published constant through default_secret_accepted_from(peer)/peer_is_recorded before the in-memory/on-disk comparisons. `git tag --contains 3767540356e16130717abe4d7846bd5a20eae71b --list 'v25.9.*'` starts at v25.9.2 and excludes v25.9.1, confirming the release boundary. `git cat-file commit 2d2d371527bde1e9d72eadcd2ee3e7c0ee3adfbc` reproduces the human-only commit-object marker check.
reasoning: The causal defect is the decision in 2d2d371 to turn a per-node random authentication credential into one source-published value shared by every installation while preserving a gate that treated knowledge of that value as a complete authenticated cluster identity. Direct parent inspection proves that credential flaw absent, and -S/-L history proves this atomic four-file version commit is the first writer rather than a move, squash aggregate, or later revert. The first-party advisory and v25.9.1 source establish exploitability, while direct fix inspection and tag containment establish closure in 25.9.2. Because the BIC commit object has only a human author/committer and no qualifying AI attribution, later AI-like signals or co-authors on fixes are irrelevant under the BIC-only rule; the correct verdict is NOT_AI.
